class: A regression guard compared only what it already knew how to measure, so a change to the words that classify a page passed unseen
symptom: Marathon's posting was read as the application's review step because of one footer sentence (f170); the replay guard, which replays 500+ saved pages through old and new code, reported nothing.
root_cause: replay_guard compared questions, concepts and answers per page, never what kind of page it was. The classification lived in a regex buried inside a Playwright method, so it could not be replayed from a saved snapshot.
why_tests_missed: The guard had no reading for page kind, and the unit tests for the classifier used hand-written pages, not the real ones.
fix: browser_automation.looks_like_posting_text() is the one function that decides 'do the words say this is a posting'; on_job_description() calls it and replay_guard reads its verdict on every saved page, so a change that flips any real page is listed before it is committed.
prevention: Put every decision that classifies a page in a pure function of the page's text, and have the regression guard replay that function, so each new decision gets a replay by construction.
